item.title: The Problem Upgrade Chart
item.description: We measure our self-worth with problems going away. But what if they don't?

item.title: Platform Investments
item.description: It's controversial, but I suggest you spend 50% of your r&d budget on your platform. Build a tech investment system that reinforces itself.

item.title: Layerinitis
item.description: Layerinitis is when teams put code where they are most comfortable while optimizing for speed vs putting the code where it belongs when considering a longer term perspective on the overall software system.

item.title: Alignment > Autonomy
item.description: It's easier to measure and feel high autonomy than it is to measure high alignment. But without alignment, autonomy is squandered.

item.title: Going fast slowly
item.description: Autonomy is great. But as you scale, the speed impact of only investing in getting fast fast will in fact slow you to a crawl.

item.title: Problem solving vs problem planning
item.description: Planning is important, but most planning is wasted time. Focus on building a problem solving culture and not a problem planning one.

item.title: Lawnmower Managers
item.description: Managing in this adult-accepting culture is a more rewarding job, and you can teach via the complex work that’s needed. You’ll have better managers for it.

item.title: Time Horizon Friction
item.description: You can cancel all your meetings, but they will come back if you don't see and squash your internal time horizon friction.
